Mempool, MEV and DEX Trades - assigned reading

questions.question_stem: Alice has pending transactions with nonces 7 and 9, but nonce 8 is missing. The nonce 9 transaction offers a much higher effective gas price. What can a builder validly do with Alice's transactions?
questions.correct_answer: Hold or ignore the nonce 9 transaction until nonce 8 is available and executable, because Alice's transactions must execute in nonce order.
incorrect_answers: Include nonce 9 before nonce 8 when its fee is high enough, because builders can reorder one sender's pending transactions for block profit.
Include nonce 7 and nonce 9 in the same block while leaving nonce 8 pending, because the missing sequence number matters only across separate blocks.
Treat nonce 9 as a replacement for nonce 7 because the later transaction pays more, even though replacement only works for the same account nonce.
questions.explanation: Builders may prioritize profitable transactions across the mempool, but transactions from the same account must respect the account's nonce sequence. Nonce gaps can leave later transactions pending even when their fees are attractive.
questions.lesson_block: A pending transaction already shows the trade
questions.specific_source_lesson: /tmp/blockchain-course-slide-only/ethereum_03-EF-ethereum_network-slides-only.qmd: Nonce ordering and replacement / Common Misconceptions And Confusions

questions.question_stem: A transaction sets maxFeePerGas to 50 gwei and maxPriorityFeePerGas to 2 gwei. If the current base fee is 30 gwei, which outcome best reflects EIP-1559 fee mechanics?
questions.correct_answer: The effective gas price is 32 gwei, the 30 gwei base fee is burned, the 2 gwei priority fee compensates the proposer, and unused max fee headroom is not paid.
incorrect_answers: The effective gas price is 50 gwei, the 30 gwei base fee is burned, and the remaining 20 gwei goes to the proposer as an extra tip, not back to the sender.
The effective gas price is 30 gwei, the base fee is burned, and no proposer tip is paid because the priority fee applies only when the cap is exceeded.
The transaction is invalid until the base fee reaches 48 gwei, because maxFeePerGas must equal the current base fee plus the stated priority fee.
questions.explanation: EIP-1559 separates the burned base fee from the priority fee. The user caps total price with maxFeePerGas, but overpayment above the current base fee plus priority fee is refunded rather than automatically spent.
questions.lesson_block: Fees set the queue: base fee burned, tip paid
questions.specific_source_lesson: /tmp/blockchain-course-slide-only/ethereum_03-EF-ethereum_network-slides-only.qmd: Fee Mechanics As Inclusion Logic And User Risk / EIP-1559 Fee Mechanics

questions.question_stem: A student says, "MEV searchers watch the Ethereum mempool, so there must be one official global queue of pending transactions." Which correction is most accurate?
questions.correct_answer: Ethereum nodes maintain local mempools that often converge through gossip but can differ, and public visibility of those local pending views creates ordering opportunities.
incorrect_answers: Ethereum nodes deterministically sort one shared pending set by effective gas price, so searchers see the same queue that builders must include in that exact order before every slot begins.
Ethereum mempools belong to consensus clients and stay hidden until attestations, so searchers learn pending intent only after finalized Beacon-chain receipts are available to users.
Private submission removes transactions from ordering games because relays must include private transactions in arrival order once a user bypasses public gossip for all builders in a slot.
questions.explanation: The lesson stresses that the mempool is not a single global queue. Public gossip makes user intent visible before inclusion, while private or direct submission changes the path through builders and relays rather than removing ordering power.
questions.lesson_block: The mempool is public, so pending trades show

questions.question_stem: In the MEV-Boost supply chain, what role separation is most accurate?
questions.correct_answer: Searchers find opportunities and submit bundles, builders assemble profitable blocks, relays validate and forward blinded bids, and validators choose a bid before receiving the full block body.
incorrect_answers: Searchers send bundles directly to validators, validators assemble the profitable block, relays only broadcast finalized receipts, and builders observe after inclusion from the network rather than bidding.
Builders choose the validator committee and sign bids for proposers, relays execute the winning block, and searchers receive priority fees from included users after the slot closes.
Relays choose the canonical block and reveal it to the network, validators only verify receipts afterward, and builders are paid for hiding transactions from searchers during block construction.
questions.explanation: Proposer-builder separation manages specialized block-building incentives by separating opportunity discovery, block assembly, bid relay, and proposer selection. It does not eliminate MEV or ordering discretion.
questions.lesson_block: Searchers, builders and relays set the order

questions.question_stem: A current Ethereum node is not just one program. Which architecture best reflects how a modern node is structured?
questions.correct_answer: A node coordinates an execution client and a consensus client, with separate responsibilities and authenticated local communication between them.
incorrect_answers: A node is a browser wallet plus a hosted RPC endpoint, where local signing replaces peer communication and the remote service performs validation.
A node is one execution client with a consensus plug-in, so the same process runs the EVM and finalizes blocks without a separate consensus client.
A node is two consensus clients paired for redundancy, with one of them exposing JSON-RPC while the other stores the EVM state database.
questions.explanation: The reading emphasizes post-Merge two-client architecture: consensus software handles agreement over chain history, execution software processes blocks and transactions, and the two coordinate locally, such as through an authenticated endpoint.

questions.question_stem: A researcher needs to query old contract storage at many historical blocks. A developer only needs convenient transaction submission through a hosted API. Which distinction between node access models matters most?
questions.correct_answer: The researcher likely needs archive-node data, while the developer can use remote access but accepts trust and privacy tradeoffs relative to operating a full node.
incorrect_answers: Both can use a default full node, because full nodes retain all historical storage while hosted APIs provide the same trust model as local validation.
The researcher can use a light client for arbitrary old storage, while the developer needs an archive node because transaction submission requires history.
A public testnet node fits both needs, because testnets mirror mainnet contract history and hosted access removes privacy tradeoffs for transactions and state queries.
questions.explanation: Chapter 3 separates full nodes, archive nodes, remote clients, and wallets by storage, verification, convenience, privacy, and trust. Archive access is about retaining historical state, while hosted APIs shift blockchain access to another node.

questions.question_stem: A team tests a trading bot only on a local blockchain simulation and a low-cost public testnet. Which limitation should they keep in mind before assuming mainnet behavior?
questions.correct_answer: Those environments are useful for development but may not reproduce mainnet congestion, real economic incentives, adversarial competition, or transaction sequencing pressure.
incorrect_answers: Local simulations are the strongest model for MEV behavior because deterministic blocks recreate other searchers and independent producers at mainnet scale in each slot.
Public testnets reproduce mainnet fee markets because test ether has equivalent economic value and creates the same liquidation competition for trading bots.
Hosted JSON-RPC access makes environments equivalent by standardizing one mempool view and one transaction ordering policy across local, testnet, and mainnet.
questions.explanation: The reading treats testnets and local simulations as valuable but limited development environments. They reduce cost and friction, yet they do not fully model mainnet incentives, congestion, adversarial behavior, or organic transaction ordering.
